title: U.S. appeals court upholds Pentagon’s Anthropic supply-chain designation
friendlyTitle: A court keeps Pentagon restrictions on Claude in place
summary: A divided federal appeals panel upheld one Pentagon designation of Anthropic as a supply-chain risk, restricting military and contractor use of Claude in Defense Department work. A separate federal court had rejected a parallel designation, and Anthropic says it is considering further review.
friendlySummary: A U.S. appeals court upheld one decision that blocks the Pentagon and its contractors from using Anthropic’s Claude for Defense Department work. Another court ruled differently on a related decision, so the legal dispute may continue.
whyItMatters: The dispute links model safeguards, government procurement and vendor access: contract terms about autonomous weapons and surveillance can now affect an AI supplier’s wider defense market. Businesses in regulated supply chains should expect model governance choices to become procurement criteria.
friendlyWhyItMatters: Rules built into an AI model can affect whether governments and contractors are allowed to buy it. Other regulated industries may face similar questions.
